node.title: Re^3: How to read compressed (gz) file in xml::twig
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [CSharma],

but script takes a lot time in providing the output

How long does it take to [man://gunzip] the file and then process it with your existing script? How much longer does the above code take? To get a somewhat decent comparison, try piping the output of [man://gunzip] into your script (it'll need a slight modification to read from STDIN).

One thing that might* speed things up is if you make use of [mod://XML::Twig]'s ability to parse an XML file in chunks, instead of reading the whole thing into memory like you're currently doing.

use warnings; use strict; use IO::Uncompress::Gunzip (); use XML::Twig; my $z = IO::Uncompress::Gunzip->new('in.xml.gz') or die "gunzip failed: $IO::Uncompress::Gunzip::GunzipError\n"; my $twig = XML::Twig->new( twig_roots => { '/CatalogListings/Offer/EstimatedCPC' => sub { my ($t, $elt) = @_; print $elt->text*100, "\n"; $t->purge; }, }, ); $twig->parse($z); $z->close;

This produces the same output as before, but discards each element when it's done processing it, and ignores the other elements.

(* The code works, but I haven't had the chance to do a performance test.)

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
